skill.displayName: Pet Picky Eater Detection | 宠物选择性拒食识别

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches a remote pet-video analysis workflow, but it silently manages identities and tokens and defaults to non-public HTTP development endpoints, which users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The published skill says default network addresses are public, but the bundled common config sets env: dev and actually resolves API bases to private HTTP addresses at 192.168.1.234. The skill also uploads local media or sends supplied URLs to external APIs without a clear privacy or retention notice.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hooks, startup registration, package-manager execution, or background workers were found. The artifact contains Python scripts, requirements files, config files, and nested shared helper modules.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions include automatic triggering for analysis and report lookup plus strong instructions to query cloud history rather than local memory. This is coherent with the report feature, but it is somewhat broad and should remain user-directed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The shared utility reads data/smyx-api-key.txt, silently creates or reuses an internal user via /sys/phoneLogin, attaches tokens and user identifiers to outbound requests, and persists user/token records in a workspace SQLite database. Identity automation is partly disclosed, but credential/token persistence and reuse are under-disclosed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact describes pet picky-eater analysis and the code submits local files or URLs to a common AI analysis API with the SMYX_PICKY_EATER_DETECTION_ANALYSIS scene code, so the generic client code is plausibly purpose-aligned with server-side analysis; historical report listing and export links are also documented.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending pet feeding videos or supplied video URLs, plus an internal user identifier, to the configured service. Review or change the config first: this package currently resolves to private HTTP development endpoints, and it may create local database records containing tokens for reuse.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the local code is generic, but it sets the specific picky-eater scene code and calls a server-side analysis API, which matches the documented remote-analysis architecture.
[YR4] unexpected: Not validated as malicious: the matched zero-width character is part of an emoji sequence in the notes table, and no offensive tooling or exploit behavior was found.
[AE1] expected: Overridden: the referenced script and API document are present locally and were inspected.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Partly accepted: report history is disclosed, but silent account bootstrap, local identity-file use, and token persistence are broader than a simple video-analysis submission flow.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted as a documentation gap: no explicit allowed-tools or permission scope is declared, despite network upload, local file reads, and local SQLite persistence.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: remote media submission is expected, but the artifact does not clearly explain privacy, retention, credential handling, token storage, or the dev HTTP endpoint behavior.
[SQP-1] expected: Mostly downgraded: the documented report triggers are generally domain-specific, though users should still confirm before cloud history lookup.
[SQP-3] expected: Low security relevance: Chinese and bilingual user-facing strings are visible throughout the artifact and do not indicate hidden or unsafe behavior.
[P9] expected: Overridden: the flagged whitespace is ordinary line wrapping/indentation in Python code, not hidden instructions.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: generic HTTP/CRUD helper methods and a broad user model exist in shared code; the active skill path mainly uses analysis, polling, page, and identity flows, but the shared authority is broader than the manifest explains.
[SDI-4] expected: Downgraded: the openclaw-agent subprocess code is commented out and not active; misleading comments alone did not create executable background-agent behavior.
[AST7] expected: Downgraded: dynamic getattr usage appears in generic ORM/data helpers and is not exposed as a user-controlled privilege boundary in the reviewed skill flow.
[E1] expected: Accepted as expected network behavior: the skill is expressly a server-side API client, but the endpoint and data-handling disclosures are insufficient.
